document: Rows that are written to the adapted marathon input although they carry one flag of the frozen row rule (analysis/adapt_combined.py ROW_RULE, `reviewed_exceptions`), reviewed one by one and cited. Lead ruling D33 of the adoption plan (2026-11-14): a deliberate, documented departure from the database lead’s rule 7 for three rows. The adapter writes a listed row only when all of this holds, and stops otherwise: the row carries the named flag, no other flag of the row rule and no pending flag; the frozen edition policy counts its edition; its finish in the release equals `finish` to the second; `edition` states the edition’s tier, its rows in the release, the official count and the coverage as the release has them; `producer_record_note` is the producer’s own note on the record; the release README still defines the flag in the words of `flag_definition`; and `external` cites the evidence (source, URL, the quoted words, who read it and when). Every other flagged row stays out. `city` is the edition’s label as the pipeline writes it; `release_city` is the release’s own key.

pace-notes-marathon-half-20261113-1113.reason: The first finisher of the 2026 London Marathon, which was won in a world record. The flag’s bound is the record that stood before this race, so it marks the race’s podium as faster than the world record. The row carries no other flag of the row rule and no pending flag, and the frozen edition policy counts its edition.
pace-notes-marathon-half-20261113-1113.producer_record_note_reading: The producer’s data-quality step (its "DQ step1" of 2026-10-10), not a disqualification: the note records the mechanical bounds the row crossed, which is why the row carries the flag.
